description: Admin screens for Solhigson apps as Razor components, rendered on the server. An app owns its routes; the package ships no page.
releaseNotes: 10.2.0: the user screens (Solhigson.Admin.Components, Solhigson.Admin.Users, Solhigson.Admin.Auditing). The users list: KitUsersList, which an app places on its own page with DetailHref (holding {id}), an optional CreateHref and a TimeZone, lists the users within the signed-in user's reach a page at a time: the name linking to the user's page with the email under it, the roles, the status (Disabled a Neutral pill, Locked out a Warn pill, No password plain text), two-factor and the last sign-in; GET filters by role, status, two-factor, no password and not signed in for 30, 90 or 180 days; and a posted search over email and user name whose text never reaches a link, a form's action, a header or the address. The user page: KitUserDetail, on a page with the user's id in its route, taking UserId, ListHref, TimeZone, CanManageAccess and CanConfigure, says first whether the user can sign in and why not, then shows Access, Two-factor (when the app registers it) and Roles; a user missing and one out of reach both answer 404, and the page must not stream. Its actions each act on the route's id alone, are refused for the viewer's own account and without their permission (a post then gets 400), are recorded through IKitAudit, and say in one alert what was done and what did not follow: with CanManageAccess, Enable, and Disable after a KitConfirm; End lockout; Send password link, for a user with no password; and Reset two-factor after a KitConfirm, which removes the authenticator and the password; with CanConfigure, the roles form, offering the roles the viewer may grant and those held, refused as stale when the roles changed since the page loaded, and saying when RoleChangeDisables makes a save disable the user; and, where the app turns on UserAdministrationOptions.AllowEmailChange, Change email, refused for a user who holds a role the viewer may not grant, the new address starting unconfirmed. User creation: KitUserCreate, with ListHref, DetailHref, CanCreate and an optional ExtraFields fragment for the app's own fields, creates a user with an email, a phone and the roles the viewer may grant, with no password and disabled while NewUserStartsDisabled is on, and asks for a password link; the user is built by the app's IKitUserFactory<TUser> (KitUserBuild.Of or KitUserBuild.Refused), else through the user type's public parameterless constructor, and an app whose rules scope users by tenant must register a factory that sets it, or every create answers NotFound. The seams: IKitUsers, which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped over the framework's UserAdministration, is how the screens read and change users (SearchAsync, GetAsync, GrantableRolesAsync, RoleNamesAsync, SetEnabledAsync, UnlockAsync, ResetTwoFactorAsync, SetRolesAsync, ChangeEmailAsync, CreateAsync, TwoFactorAvailable, SignInNeedsConfirmedEmail; with KitUserSearch, KitUserPage, KitUserLookup, KitUserRow, KitRoleNames, KitUserResult, KitNewUser, KitUserMessages and KitUserAudit's users.* actions), and throws nothing but the caller's cancellation; IKitSessions (Ends, EndAsync) and IKitUserNotices (PasswordLinkNeededAsync, AccessChangedAsync, TwoFactorResetAsync, EmailChangedAsync), which an app registers to end sessions in its own store and to send the link and the notices, and whose defaults answer false and warn once a process, so the screens tell the administrator what to send and how long an open session lasts, read from the security stamp validation interval and the application cookie; and IKitUserFactory<TUser>. One rule names the acting user for the users seam and the audit seam alike: the first claim of Identity's ClaimsIdentity.UserIdClaimType, counted only from a signed-in identity. Changes for a 10.1.0 app: the audit seam's actor, when the actor provider gives the unattributed one, now follows that rule, so the sub fallback is gone and an app whose tokens carry the id as sub sets UserIdClaimType to sub; AddSolhigsonAdmin now also registers IKitUsers, so it registers IKitMenuSource, IKitAudit, IHttpContextAccessor and IKitUsers, each kept when the app registered it first; KitAuditEvent's payload holds no personal value but users.email-changed's previous address; and KitAuditFailed names the exception's type only, never its message. KitHref.LocalOrThrow gains an overload taking what the value must be (KitHref.MustPost, KitHref.MustLink), KitPageHeader gains LineContent, KitFilterBar gains Id, and kit.manifest.json gains the kit-user and kit-users names. The README lists each log line the screens and seams write, its level and what to do, beside the framework's user_administration and two_factor counters on the meter Solhigson.Framework.Identity. The user pages refuse framing, as the settings page does: the app sends X-Frame-Options: DENY and Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' on them, and the components set no header. With AllowEmailChange on, one administrator holding both CanConfigure and CanManageAccess can take over any account within reach whose roles they may grant: move its address, then send a password link or reset its two-factor. Where the app's own sign-in sends a password reset to an address it has not confirmed, the address change alone is enough, needing CanConfigure only, and giving the two permissions to different roles does not guard it: gate that reset on a confirmed address (an email change leaves the new one unconfirmed), or keep AllowEmailChange off. Otherwise an app guards by giving the two permissions to different roles. Registering IKitUserNotices tells the previous address, after the fact. Minor bump: every type and member is new but for those four changes. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.27.0 or later. 10.1.0: the settings screen, the package's first screen (Solhigson.Admin.Components, Solhigson.Admin.Settings, Solhigson.Admin.Auditing). KitSettingsEditor, which an app places on a page of its own with its route and [Permission], lists every setting the app's catalogue declares, one section a group in the order the catalogue registered them, under a Settings header that counts them and links to a needs-attention view, with a GET filter over key, name and purpose, never a value. CanEdit, false unless set, comes from a second permission: without it no form renders, a post is the framework's 400 and a Personal value shows as Hidden; a Secret's value is never written into the page. With it each line is a form of its own that saves or resets that setting through Core's SaveDeclaredSettingAsync and ResetDeclaredSettingAsync and says the outcome at the line: saved, reset, no change, a refusal beside the field in the screen's words with what was typed kept (never a secret's), changed since the page loaded, failed with no exception text, and a Warn alert when other instances were not told and may show the old value until their settings cache recovers. Under the groups, Rows with no declaration lists each stored row no declared setting matches, by name and flag pills, never a value; with CanEdit each has a Remove that opens one KitConfirm saying older code may still read the row by name and the screen cannot put it back, and its confirm calls RemoveUndeclaredRowAsync. Above the groups a warning says a secret's save is refused while the legacy encryptor is in force. The setting field: KitSettingField renders one KitSetting (KitSetting.From(DeclaredSettingLine)) with one control of its kind: a Switch a toggle that submits its form when it changes (a Save in noscript otherwise), a number with min, max and step, a Duration an amount and a unit or one text field, a List a textarea, a Text a text field; a Secret, a row stored sensitive and a masked line an empty password field, with no value or mask in the markup; with ReadOnly, Fields, Error and ChildContent. KitSettingValue.Compose turns the posted KitSettingFields into the setting's stored text or a refusal sentence (KitSettingComposed), never an exception, and Fill gives each control's starting values. The audit seam: IKitAudit (Records, and RecordAsync answering whether a row was written), which AddSolhigsonAdmin registers scoped as KitAudit<TContext>, resolving the audit service, the actor provider and the context from the request at first use; KitAuditEvent and KitAuditActions. Each save, reset and removal done is recorded as a SecurityEvent on AppSetting, settings.saved, settings.reset or settings.stray-removed, with the actor and a payload of the key and the values before and after as the framework's result shows them, the mask for a Secret, a row stored sensitive and a Personal value. A removed stray row stored plain under a plain name keeps its raw value in the append-only audit row: only a row stored sensitive or under a secret-looking name is masked. When Records is false (no audit service resolves, or the context maps no AuditTrail and no IAuditSink is registered) the screen says changes here leave no audit record and one Warning is logged a process; a record that fails logs one Error and says so at the line, and the change is not undone. TContext must be registered scoped. KitConfirm gains OnConfirm and KitDialog OnSubmit, so a confirm's form is handled by the component that owns it; kit.forms.js submits the form of a data-kit-submit-on-change control and keeps one such post in flight a page; the gallery gains a settings section; kit.manifest.json gains the kit-setting and kit-settings names. The README documents the app's page and every log line the screen, the seam and a save write. Minor bump: every type and member is new, and no existing component's behaviour changes. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.27.0 or later. 10.0.0: the first release of Solhigson.Admin, the admin kit: Razor components for Solhigson apps, rendered statically on the server, with no interactive render mode and no inline script; an app owns every route, and the package holds components and no screen yet. Head and theme: KitHead, first in <head>, links the kit's stylesheet and scripts with the page's nonce where its policy uses one; KitTheme reads the viewer's light or dark choice from its cookie on the server, with KitTheme.HtmlAttributes(HttpContext) for <html>, and KitThemeSwitch offers the choice. Components: KitButton, KitStatusPill and KitAlert; KitField, one field for every input kind; KitDialog (a modal or a drawer) and KitConfirm on the native <dialog>; KitMenu, KitMenuItem and KitMenuForm, a row menu on the native popover; KitShell, the admin layout with a skip link, a side rail, a top bar with the user's menu (the theme choices and sign-out) and the main region; KitPageHeader, KitLead, KitEmptyState and KitPager; KitTable with KitColumn, and KitFilterBar, Get or Post; KitMark; and KitGallery, every component in every state on fixed example data, for a page an app adds in development or behind a permission. Links: every url a kit component takes goes through KitHref: a ~/ path is joined to the path base; a button's or a link menu item's Href may also be an https:// address (KitHref.LocalOrHttps), and a form's action is local alone (KitHref.Local). Menu: IKitMenuSource builds the shell's menu from the permissions the signed-in user's roles hold, read through PermissionManager's cached reads, and AddSolhigsonAdmin<TUser, TContext>() or AddSolhigsonAdmin<TUser, TKey, TContext>() registers it; the menu shows, each page's [Permission] enforces. Styles: tokens for every colour, size, space, radius, shadow, duration, curve and font, light and dark, in layers (kit.tokens, kit.base, kit.components) that an app's app layer overrides, each name listed in kit.manifest.json, a name leaving which is a breaking change; every motion reads a duration token that is 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion. Rules: the package's tests hold its markup, scripts and stylesheets to no inline script, style or handler, no other host, every href and form action through KitHref, measured contrast pairs, and no colour, length or duration outside the tokens. Depends on Solhigson.Framework.Core 10.24.0 or later.
